A Fast-Time-Constant (FTC) circuit is a short time constant differentiator circuit located between the Video Detector and the input to the first video amplifier. When a large block of video is applied to the FTC circuit, only the leading edge will pass...

Gated AGC will not respond to jamming pulses that arrive outside the gating period. Without gated AGC, jamming signals would cause the AGC to follow the interfering signal rather than the real target signal return...

Gated AGC and Fast-Time-Constant (FTC) circuits are used to overcome the effects of Electromagnetic Interference jamming. A gated AGC circuit permits signals that occur only in a very short time interval (gating period) to develop the AGC...

STC decreases the amplitude of nearby object return signals, while IAGC decreases the amplitude of larger-than average return signals. Signal returns between the extremes are easily compensated for by the combination of STC and IAGC...

At the end of the transmitted pulse, the STC voltage begins to rise, gradually increasing the receiver gain to maximum. The combination of STC and IAGC circuits result in better overall receiver performance...

STC circuits apply a bias voltage that varies with time, to the IF Amplifiers in order to control receiver gain. When the transmitter fires, the STC circuit decreases the receiver gain to zero to prevent the amplification of any transmitter leakage energy and high-energy sea return.../

signals is not the best adjustment for distant object return signals. Sensitivity Time-Control (STC) circuits are used to adjust amplifier gain to time (range) during a single pulse repetition period.
The automatic gain control can be shutoff to allow an operator to manually adjust the receiver gain for the best reception of a particular signal.

Automatic Gain Control (AGC) and Instantaneous Automatic Gain Control (IAGC) circuits produce a voltage proportional to the average strength of the detected signal and noise. The gain of the IF amplifier automatically varies with changes in the RADAR return signal amplitude...

RADAR receiver performance can be degraded due to unfavorable weather conditions, sea returns and Electromagnetic interference from external sources such as Electronic Counter Measures (ECM) jamming.g.
A Video Mixer may be used to combine the video signal and other RADAR information such as ship or aircraft heading markers and range markers.

The Video Processor is used to analyze and shape the video signal before it is applied to the other circuits. The Video Processor forces a received signal to meet certain requirements prior to its acceptance as a valid target return...

The most critical stage of a RADAR receiver's IF section is the input or first stage. The characteristics of this stage determine the noise figure and the sensitivity with respect to detecting small objects at long ranges...

The IF amplifier determines the receiver's gain, signal-to-noise ratio, and effective bandwidth. The typical IF Amplifier contains three to ten amplifier stages each with sufficient gain to accommodate the expected echo signal power...
The crystal rectifiers are nonlinear devices, and the output from each crystal is an IF signal equal to the difference between the local oscillator frequency and the incoming echo signal frequency...

If the local oscillator frequency is 3 GHz (3000 MHz), a frequency shift of just 0.1 percent would be a 3 MHz frequency shift. This could equal the bandwidth of the receiver and cause considerable loss in gain...

Blocking occurs when the voltage pulse at the RADAR receiver input is too large or a portion of the transmit pulse leaks into the receiver input. As a result, the receiver for a short time, is insensitive to signals below a certain level and may not show small, nearby objects. Tunnel-diodes, Traveling Wave Tube's (TWT) and parametric microwave amplifiers are used as low-noise, high-gain RF Amplifiers. When external noise is negligible, the noise generated by the input stage of the receiver determines the receiver sensitivity...

The term Dynamic Range is applied to RADAR receivers. It identifies the difference, in decibels, between the largest signal the receiver can handle without saturating, and the minimum discernable signal it can detect...

The receiver must be selective to the point that it amplifies only the echo signals generated from its associated transmitter. At the same time, the receiver must be able to accurately track the transmitter in frequency because drift would degrade echo reception...

The RADAR receiver must accomplish this amplification with minimum introduction of noise voltages. In addition to having a high gain and low noise ratio, the receiver must provide sufficient bandwidth to pass the many harmonics contained in the echo signal...

RADAR receivers are sensitive enough to accept signals in the order of picowatts and amplify them in many useful ways. The weaker the signal, which a receiver can accept and efficiently display, the greater the effective range of the RADAR...

Remember, the charging diode prevents the PFN from discharging through the power supply. Because there is currently no discharge path, the PFN will be held off, and maintain its charge (Point A) until a discharge path is presented...

As the magnetic field collapses, it adds another charge equal to 90% of the power supplies potential to the PFN. Thus, the PFN stores a charge equal to 180% (or 1.8 times) the total power supply potential...

When the PFN reaches 90% of the power supply's potential, the reduced current can no longer maintain the magnetic field in the charging choke. Without current flow to sustain the field, it collapses...

As the power supply output begins to charge the Pulse Forming Network (PFN), the current flow causes a strong magnetic filed in the charging choke. When the charge in the PFN approaches the power supply potential, current in the circuit begins to decrease...

An electronic element, such as a thyratron or Silicon Controlled Rectifier (SCR) is used as a switch in pulsed RADARs. When the switch is closed, a low-impedance discharge path is provided for the storage device through the pulse transformer....

The load for the modulator is a high-power transmitter tube (TWT). The modulator output is coupled to the load via a pulse transformer that compensates for impedance mismatches. The use of a pulse transformer allows the DC to charge the storage device...

A charging choke aids the charging of the PFN and controls charge time. The charging diode prevents the PFN from discharging through the power supply and holds off the PFN discharge until the switch closes...
